summary: The human brain is the substrate for every thought, movement, perception, and emotion we have. But too much of a clinician's day is still spent on everything around the care. From intraoperative judgment calls to the documentation and coordination that follow, that's the daily calculus for a neurosurgeon — and AI now has an opportunity to improve how it all gets done. Healthcare is a multi-trillion dollar industry largely built on workflows designed decades ago. Data lives on different systems, on paper, or in a surgeon's head. The technology to capture clinical notes during surgery, interpret medical imaging, and forecast how a mass might evolve — that's not science fiction. It's possible. summary: When someone calls 211 in a crisis, seconds matter. See how United Way cut wait times from 11 minutes to under 2 with Amazon Connect. United Way is an essential part of the care coordination ecosystem, the virtual front door for people in crisis. But the system they inherited in 2023 was fragmented. The average wait time was 11 minutes, with one in five callers giving up before reaching anyone. After moving to Amazon Connect, United Way cut that wait time to under two minutes and now sees full completion of the calls they receive. For the people on the other end of the line, like a single mother calling for emergency shelter, it means reaching real help when it matters most, and knowing they're not alone. This is a Moments That Matter story about what changes when the technology behind a crisis line finally matches what's at stake. summary: In this episode of Napkin to MVP, the founder of Dedalus Labs shares how a conviction that nobody else was building the right future for AI agents turned into a research lab, a pivot, and eventually the compute substrate for an agent-native world. It's the unpolished story of going from an idea on a napkin to virtual machines that boot in 50 milliseconds, built for agentic workloads that need to be persistent, fast, and always on. The team started by building agent infrastructure, but quickly learned the primitive underneath wasn't good enough. Users hated their existing sandboxes. So Dedalus built their own VM from scratch, shipping a first MVP in two weeks with a 2-3 second cold start, then obsessively optimizing it down to 150 milliseconds, then 50. Along the way, the team faced the classic founder question: when is it good enough to ship? For Dedalus, the answer was always "not yet." Starting with credits through AWS Activate, Dedalus has been working closely with the AWS team from day one. Today, Dedalus Machines sits on top of EC2 and S3, and every new Dedalus customer becomes an AWS customer by default. This is what building with AI on AWS looks like for startups: infrastructure so fast and reliable that nobody even notices it's there, powering the agents that will define the next era of computing. AWS gives founders the AI, compute, and infrastructure to go from idea to impact faster. ▶ Read the full founder story: https://aws.amazon.com/aws-startups/learn/founders-st
title: Dedalus Labs: Building the Compute Layer for Every AI Agent | AWS Startups | Amazon Web Services

summary: DynamoDB offers zero infrastructure management, instant scaling, pay-per-request billing, and no cold starts, upgrades, or maintenance windows. These capabilities, along with native vector search, make DynamoDB ideal for agentic applications that need semantic retrieval. For globally distributed applications, DynamoDB global tables is a multi-Region, multi-active database with up to 99.999% availability. It supports multi-Region strong consistency enabling your applications to always stay available and read the same data from any Region, so you can build zero recovery point objective applications. A broad set of DynamoDB security controls and compliance standards satisfy the requirements for governments, global banks, and other high-sensitivity organizations.
